data.analysis: Choose N=3 for three distinct avenues in the supplied pixel-independent, iteration-heavy kernel: thread-level load balance, packed SIMD, and scalar instruction-level parallelism. These mechanisms may interact, so measured gains must not be assumed additive; retain Mother’s integration and confirmation time. The supplied baseline is correct and has three measured times (mean 0.563421510301172 s), but its serial source ignores `threads` and the observations provide no separate one-/four-core results. This is a development baseline, not independent confirmation. The execution record establishes x86_64 and the official statement supplies EPYC 9654/GCC 14.2; no ROMEO inspection tool was exposed, and actual compiler ISA flags/features remain unverified. Each tree should keep changes to `src/candidate.cpp`, preserve exact output for all valid inputs and shifted bounds, and compare native time at one and four cores without changing the protocol. Only correctly validated and independently confirmed measured candidates should enter final G; measure the combined program rather than inferring its speed from its parts.

children.objective: Explore row-level OpenMP work distribution on the supplied scalar recurrence. Compare suitable static and dynamic/guided row schedules and chunk sizes, with a serial path for a one-thread budget if it avoids overhead. Never create more than `threads` workers or change global OpenMP settings. Keep per-pixel float operation order and iteration behavior unchanged, write every output element, and do not specialize to benchmark bounds or dimensions. Measure one- and four-core cases, especially load balance and scheduling overhead at n=1024; validate smaller and shifted-bound cases before comparing performance.
children.subject: Thread-budgeted OpenMP row scheduling

children.objective: Develop an exact SIMD kernel across adjacent x pixels, using only ISA support appropriate to the frozen target/build. Explore active-lane handling for different escape counts and correct tail processing; do not use approximate membership tests or change compiler flags. Preserve the scalar recurrence’s float semantics and verify exact iteration counts against the correctness protocol, including smaller sizes and shifted bounds. Measure one- and four-core results and report any ISA/build assumptions or failures; avoid folding in a separate scheduling optimization so the SIMD contribution remains identifiable.
children.subject: Exact SIMD across independent pixels

children.objective: Explore scalar multi-pixel interleaving (for example, small groups of independent pixel states) to expose instruction-level parallelism while retaining scalar arithmetic—no explicit SIMD intrinsics or OpenMP scheduling changes. Preserve each pixel’s escape check, count, and float operation order, handle group tails, and overwrite the complete output. Do not use approximations or specialize to n, parameter, or bounds. Validate shifted and smaller cases, and measure the one-thread kernel as the main comparison; report its four-core-budget result transparently without claiming thread scaling.
children.subject: Scalar instruction-level parallelism via pixel interleaving
